one_liner: Private journaling app with on-device encryption, no account required, and AI reflections that never leave your phone.
description: quietpage is a journaling app for people who won't put their inner life in someone's cloud. Entries are encrypted on-device with keys that never leave the phone, no account or email is required to start, and the optional AI reflection feature runs a local model so prompts and entries are never transmitted anywhere. Export is plain Markdown, always.
target_user: Privacy-conscious people who journal or want to start

icp.who: Privacy-minded professionals and journaling enthusiasts who distrust cloud-synced diaries
icp.pain: Existing journals want an account and cloud sync, which is exactly where you don't want your most private writing
icp.buying_trigger: A data-breach headline or a therapist's journaling suggestion colliding with distrust of cloud diary apps

differentiators: End-to-end on-device encryption with keys that never leave the device — no account, no email, no server
AI reflections computed by a local model, so entries are never transmitted
Plain Markdown export with zero lock-in
proof_points: 1,900 downloads in the first month with no paid marketing
Recommended in r/privacy weekly software thread
Full security model documented on the site, including key storage details
pricing_current: paid ($4.99 one-time on the App Store)

voice.sample_phrase: Your thoughts stay on your phone. Full stop.

signals: Live on the App Store with a one-time price

gaps: No screenshots of the reflection feature on the site

confidence.notes: Privacy architecture is documented in detail. Traction is early and modest, consistent with a recent indie launch.
